title: Tenant support ticket contracts and governed routing evidence

phases.objective: Recover the missing tenant support-ticket API contracts, deterministic routing evidence, and the bounded dependency-injection correction required to test routing without database credentials or repair authority.

e2e_journeys.actor: authenticated tenant user and support contract reviewer
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Tenant support-ticket create, list, detail, and event contracts plus the routing-resolution test harness
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The four tenant routes are precisely documented, resolution output remains sanitized and role-gated, same-tenant delivery is limited to owners and admins, platform escalation remains separately classified, and an injected connection is honored without initializing the default database pool.
steps: Load the canonical split support-ticket contract and precise route registry entries.
Validate create-or-dedupe, tenant-scoped list, role-gated detail, and customer-visible event contracts.
Inject a bounded in-memory connection into the routing service without database environment variables.
Resolve routing recipients for a tenant member through the runtime service test harness.
Verify same-tenant queries restrict recipients to owner and admin roles.
Verify platform-admin escalation is retained as a separate route class.
Regenerate and verify frontend governance and dispatch evidence from the reconciled exact-head sources.
assertions: POST and GET /me/support/tickets are registered through the precise contract registry.
GET /me/support/tickets/{ticket_id} exposes resolution details only under the documented tenant admin or owner boundary.
POST /me/support/tickets/{ticket_id}/events appends customer-visible evidence without provider dispatch or external delivery.
Resolution summaries are sanitized evidence and never authorize or apply a repair.
An explicitly injected connection is used before any default getPool initialization, so the synthetic routing regression requires no DB credentials.
Same-tenant routing recipients are restricted to owner and admin roles.
Platform-admin escalation remains separately classified from same-tenant delivery.
The support resolution test is discoverable through the canonical composed test manifest.
Generated frontend governance and dispatch evidence is deterministic for the exact candidate head.
No migration, SQL execution, deployment, credential access, provider call, external email send, Production mutation, or force-push occurs.

phases.objective: Observe tenant support-ticket contract usage and routing evidence after merge without enabling external delivery or repair mutation.

Exercise malformed ticket identifiers, stale resolution evidence, missing tenant membership, unavailable routing metadata, and invalid injected connection contracts through bounded fail-closed responses.
Verify the recovered contracts against a controlled non-production tenant after any separately authorized migration and deployment steps.
Require production runtime parity and post-deployment readback before treating the recovered contracts as operational production evidence.
